The AGA-Att mechanism can be viewed as a low-rank spatial interaction bottleneck: graph tokens first project information to a small set of shared agent tokens and then receive redistributed summaries from them. Apparently, by reducing the number of direct interactions between input tokens, the above mechanism can lower the computational cost from O ​ ( N 2 ) O(N^{2}) to O ​ ( N ​ a ) O(Na) , where N N is the number of input tokens and a a is the number of agent tokens ( a ≪ N a\ll N ). This design is most effective when node-level temporal behaviors contain shared modes (i.e., spatial redundancy), so that the node representation manifold can be well-approximated by a limited number of latent prototypes.
